source_title: Diljit Dosanjh takes dig at concert critics
source_excerpt: Diljit Dosanjh has spoken about the uncertainty surrounding his Delhi concert, taking a dig at those who allegedly attempted to prevent the event. The singer performed at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on October 30, after the show faced questions over police permission. Following the performance, he shared several moments from the concert on social media. He also thanked his audience and made pointed remarks about those who reportedly wanted the event cancelled.Diljit Dosanjh celebrates Delhi concert and thanks fansAfter completing the performance, Diljit Dosanjh posted a glimpse of his introductory shot from the concert. The singer used the post to acknowledge the audience's support and celebrate his show in the national capital.He wrote, "Spread the love, folks! Dosanjhwala has hit the big time in Delhi. Just sit back and wonderâ¦ how did this happen? Love my fans!"Singer takes a dig at those who allegedly tried to stop the showDiljit Dosanjh also addressed the reported attempts to prevent the concert from taking place. Rather than naming anyone, the singer made a reference to the people he believed had worked against the event.He used humour to describe a conversation with God ahead of the performance. Recalling the exchange, Diljit wrote, "I even had a direct word with God about this! I spoke to Him over the phone. I told Him, 'Thereâs a show coming up...' Some people really tried hard to make sure the show wouldn't happen!"Diljit Dosanjh jokes about rain during Delhi performanceThe singer also mentioned the weather while sharing his thoughts about the show. He appeared to have hoped that rainfall would not disrupt the performance or affect the audience's experience.Diljit wrote, "May God hold back the rain for 3-4 hours. Love my fans! I donât bother responding to what many people say, because I donât consider them worth my time. Donât you worry, weâre going to absolutely crush it."His message combined a request for favorable weather with a response to his critics. He also assured his followers that he was focused on delivering the performance.Delhi Police initially withheld permission for the concertThe October 30 concert at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium had faced uncertainty after the Delhi Police initially denied permission. Officials cited specific threat-related inputs and security concerns. They also pointed to law-and-order responsibilities during the festive season.The development raised concerns among ticket-holders, who were waiting to know whether the event would proceed. The uncertainty also placed the concert's schedule under scrutiny, as attendees had already made plans to be present.Organisers secure clearance after discussions with policeAccording to The Hindu, the organisers subsequently held discussions with the Delhi Police to address the concerns. They presented additional arrangements covering crowd control, traffic management and public safety.Following these discussions, the authorities reconsidered the matter and granted permission for the event.
